name: Camera Pose and Extrinsic/Intrinsic Optimization
text:
# Camera Pose and Extrinsic/Intrinsic Optimization


## Overview
This family of methods addresses the problem of optimizing camera parameters (extrinsics and intrinsics) simultaneously with [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) weights, eliminating the reliance on pre-computed [Structure-from-Motion (SfM)](#16341-structure-from-motion-sfm.md) pipelines like COLMAP [G]. By treating camera poses as learnable parameters, these methods enable 3D reconstruction from sparse or uncalibrated image sets [G]. What sets this family apart from siblings like [Time-dependent NeRF with Continuous Camera Motion](12399-time-dependent-nerf-with-continuous-camera-motion.md) is the explicit optimization of discrete camera poses per image rather than continuous motion functions, and from [Camera Preconditioning](12545-camera-preconditioning.md) by focusing on the joint gradient-based update of poses and scene geometry rather than preconditioning the optimizer for faster convergence [G].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the core mechanism of [differentiable rendering](#16276-differentiable-rendering.md), where the rendered pixel color $\hat{C}(r)$ is a differentiable function of the camera pose $P$ and the [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) parameters $\Theta$ [G]. The optimization problem is typically formulated as minimizing a loss function $\mathcal{L}$ with respect to both $\Theta$ and $P$:
$$ \min_{\Theta, P} \mathcal{L}(\hat{C}(r; \Theta, P), C(r)) $$
where $C(r)$ is the ground-truth pixel color [G]. The gradient $\nabla_P \mathcal{L}$ allows the camera pose to be updated via an optimizer (e.g., Adam, [SGD](#15522-sgd-street-view-synthesis-with-gaussian-splatting-and-diffus.md)) in lockstep with the NeRF weights [G]. Key shared components include:
1. **Ray Casting:** Computing ray origins $\hat{o}$ and directions $\hat{d}$ from pixel coordinates using current camera estimates [G]. For a [pinhole camera model](#4037-perspective-projection-of-points.md) with focal length $f$ and [rotation](#19376-rotation.md) $R$ and translation $t$:
$$ \hat{o} = t $$
$$ \hat{d} = R \begin{pmatrix} (u - W/2)/f \\ -(v - H/2)/f \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} $$
2. **Differentiable Rendering:** The [volume rendering integral](#8682-volume-rendering-integral.md) is computed via discrete summation, allowing backpropagation through the [ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md) process to the pose parameters [G].
3. **Joint Optimization:** Separate optimizers or a combined optimizer are used to update NeRF weights and pose parameters, often with different learning rates to stabilize convergence [G].

## Subtopics

### [NeRF with Unknown Camera Parameters](7405-nerf-with-unknown-camera-parameters.md)
Simultaneously optimizes camera poses and NeRF parameters without pre-estimated poses, eliminating the need for external SfM pipelines. Choose this for sparse forward-facing views where intrinsics and extrinsics are unknown.

### [Hybrid 2D/3D Registration Optimization Pipeline](8120-hybrid-2d-3d-registration-optimization-pipeline.md)
Estimates 6-DoF pose of a 2D X-ray relative to a 3D CT volume using a two-stage differentiable network similarity loss and Grad-NCC refinement. Choose this for medical image registration tasks requiring global convergence and [local refinement](#23548-user-defined-roi-refinement.md).

### [NoPe-NeRF](8705-nope-nerf.md)
Optimizes relative poses between consecutive frames using undistorted [monocular depth priors](#12353-monocular-depth-estimation-adaptation-and-supervision.md) and a point cloud loss, avoiding global alignment or iterative refinement. Choose this for monocular video sequences where depth priors can guide relative pose estimation.

### [AltNeRF](8763-altnerf.md)
Creates resilient NeRFs from monocular videos using self-supervised monocular depth estimation to generate depth and pose priors, harmonizing NeRF outputs with priors through error-tolerant regularization. Choose this when explicit 3D supervision is unavailable and initial poses are imprecise.

### [Vision-Only Pose Filtering in a NeRF](10501-vision-only-pose-filtering-in-a-nerf.md)
Estimates 6-DoF pose and velocities of a robot within a NeRF using only monocular RGB images via recursive Bayesian estimation, balancing photometric and dynamics prediction losses. Choose this for robot state estimation in low-gradient regions where single-shot estimators fail.

### [Online Receding Horizon Replanning](10509-online-receding-horizon-replanning.md)
A vision-based robot navigation pipeline combining trajectory planning and pose filtering in a receding horizon loop for dynamic maneuvering with uncertain initial poses. Choose this for dynamic environments where the robot must change homotopy classes around obstacles in response to disturbances.

### [NeRF-based Trajectory Optimization](10632-nerf-based-trajectory-optimization.md)
Optimizes dense flat output waypoints directly using first-order gradient descent, using NeRF density as an implicit obstacle representation for collision-free paths. Choose this for differentially flat systems navigating narrow spaces without closed-form polytopes.

### [MELON](11909-melon.md)
Jointly optimizes NeRF and camera poses from unposed images using a "modulo loss" to handle rotational symmetries in the $SO(3)$ latent space, enabling ab-initio reconstruction without pose initialization. Choose this for object-centric reconstruction where adversarial approaches fail and pre-trained CNNs are unavailable.

### [Time-dependent NeRF with Continuous Camera Motion](12399-time-dependent-nerf-with-continuous-camera-motion.md)
Jointly optimizes a [time-dependent NeRF and continuous camera motion](#12399-time-dependent-nerf-with-continuous-camera-motion.md) from monocular video using local [SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md) and appearance fields, modeling motion as continuous velocities. Choose this for dynamic scenes where discrete pose parameters cause local minima.

### [Camera Preconditioning](12545-camera-preconditioning.md)
Normalizes and decorrelates camera parameters during optimization using a preconditioner matrix derived from projection derivative covariance, addressing ill-conditioning from mixed units or correlations. Choose this when naive optimization fails due to correlated coefficients or differing parameter scales.

### [SPARF](12705-sparf.md)
Joint [pose-NeRF training](#12705-sparf.md) for sparse views with noisy poses, enforcing multi-view geometry constraints (correspondence and depth consistency) to prevent overfitting. Choose this for novel view synthesis from as few as 3 input views with large viewpoint variations.

### [Test-Time Two-Stage Optimization](13119-test-time-two-stage-optimization.md)
Post-training procedure decoupling pose refinement and appearance adaptation into two sequential stages to handle varying lighting and transient objects. Choose this for unconstrained image collections where single-stage optimization fails to separate pose and appearance changes.

### [Joint Pose and Radiance Field Optimization](17928-joint-pose-and-radiance-field-optimization.md)
Reconstructs 3D scenes from unposed images by simultaneously optimizing NeRF and camera extrinsic/intrinsic parameters, treating poses as learnable variables. Choose this when the dependency between pose estimation and scene modeling must be resolved jointly.

### [Sync-NeRF Offset Optimization](17949-sync-nerf-offset-optimization.md)
Reconstructs dynamic scenes from unsynchronized multi-view videos by introducing learnable per-camera time offsets to align temporal axes. Choose this for multi-view video capture where cameras are not temporally synchronized.

#### NeRF Registration
A rigid NeRF registration method that minimizes a photometric loss between rendered images from two NeRFs, using VF and Normalizing Flows to guide ray sampling and generate novel views [S1]. Optimizes a 6-DoF rigid transformation parameter (rotation and translation) to align the two NeRFs, minimizing a photometric loss between rendered images [S1]. Uses a learnable scale factor added to the 6-DoF parameters to handle unknown scale and illumination changes [S1]. Photometric loss is susceptible to inaccuracies on textureless surfaces, high symmetry can cause 180° convergence errors, and partial overlap or moving objects are not explicitly handled [S1].

#### Progressive Camera Pose Generation
A training strategy that gradually increases the angular distance of sampled target viewpoints from source views to stabilize optimization [S2, unofficial]. Samples noise uniformly from interval $[-\beta, +\beta]$ and adds it to original Euler rotation angles of input view poses [S2, unofficial]. Parameter $\beta$ grows linearly from 3 to 9 degrees throughout optimization [S2, unofficial].

#### NeRF Pose Optimization
Formulates pose reconstruction as an inverse problem by optimizing the pose instead of network parameters given a pre-trained NeRF [S1]. Uses the photo-metric loss Eq. 6 to optimize the pose [S1]. Uses an interest-point detector and performs interest region-based sampling [S1].

#### Camera Pose Optimization and Perturbation
Two CameraOptModule instances: one for [random pose perturbation](#11415-random-pose-perturbation.md) during training, and one for learnable pose adjustment, both applied per image [S4, unofficial]. Initializes perturbation module with random noise scaled by `cfg.pose_noise` [S4, unofficial]. Initializes adjustment module with zero parameters to ensure neutral initial pose [S4, unofficial]. During training, applies perturbation to `camtoworlds` if `cfg.pose_noise > 0`: `camtoworlds = self.pose_perturb(camtoworlds, image_ids)` [S4, unofficial]. Applies learnable adjustment to `camtoworlds` if `cfg.pose_opt` is enabled: `camtoworlds = self.pose_adjust(camtoworlds, image_ids)` [S4, unofficial]. `cfg.pose_opt_lr`: Base learning rate for pose adjustment; actual LR is `cfg.pose_opt_lr * sqrt(batch_size)` [S4, unofficial]. `cfg.pose_opt_reg`: Weight decay for the pose optimizer [S4, unofficial]. `cfg.pose_noise`: Magnitude of random pose perturbation applied during training [S4, unofficial].

## Background
The problem of joint pose and NeRF optimization emerged as a solution to the dependency on accurate Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipelines like COLMAP, which can fail on sparse or uncalibrated image sets [G]. Early work, such as iNeRF (December 2020) [166], formulated pose reconstruction as an inverse problem given a pre-trained NeRF, optimizing poses using photo-metric loss and interest-point-based sampling [S1]. Given a pre-trained NeRF, K. Gao, et al. using the photo-metric loss Eq. 6, Yen-Chen et al. optimized the pose instead of the network parameters [S1]. The authors used an interest-point detector and performed interest region-based sampling [S1]. The authors also performed semi-supervised experiments, where they used iNeRF pose estimation on unposed training images to augment the NeRF training set, and further train the forward NeRF [S1]. Subsequently, NeRF– (February 2021) [101] jointly estimated NeRF model parameters and camera parameters, allowing for end-to-end construction of radiance fields and novel view synthesis, achieving results comparable to using COLMAP with the 2020 NeRF model [S1].
